execution_overview.overall_summary: The agent executed both active candidates for Hendricks_QuartJournEco_2018_wNKW_path03 inside Docker. Both tasks estimated positive no-high-school versus college-degree log wage gain coefficients after the planned 1%/99% log-wage-gain trimming, supporting the focal claim that immigrants who have never been to high school gain more on migration to the United States than immigrants with a college degree. Both results were statistically strong with p < 0.05.

method_fidelity.fidelity_note: The agent followed the planned Task1 path exactly: it used the authorized wage_gain_table.xlsx dataset, constructed log wage gain and education groups, applied the planned 1%/99% trimming rule, and estimated the planned adjusted OLS model with HC1 robust standard errors. No implementation repairs were needed.

result_raw.result_text: In the adjusted trimmed OLS model, immigrants with no high school had higher log wage gains than immigrants with a college degree: coefficient = 0.263, corresponding to about 30.0% higher wage gains, p = 0.0036.

conclusion.rule_applied: The fixed conclusion rule was applied: a positive no_high_school coefficient relative to college_degree supports the focal claim; p < 0.05 indicates strong statistical evidence, while uncertainty is reported separately.
conclusion.uncertainty_statement: The estimate provides strong support because it is positive, p < 0.05, and the 95% confidence interval excludes zero in the expected positive direction.
conclusion.conclusion_text: Task1 supports the focal claim: after adjustment and planned trimming, no-high-school immigrants had larger wage gains than college-degree immigrants.

method_fidelity.fidelity_note: The agent followed the planned Task2 path exactly: it used the authorized pooled poor-country wage-gain file including Mexico, constructed log wage gain and education groups, applied the planned 1%/99% trimming rule, and estimated the planned unadjusted OLS model with HC1 robust standard errors and no prohibited controls. No implementation repairs were needed.

result_raw.result_text: In the unadjusted trimmed OLS model using the authorized pooled poor-country sample including Mexico, immigrants with no high school had higher log wage gains than immigrants with a college degree: coefficient = 0.348, corresponding to about 41.6% higher wage gains, p = 0.0009.

conclusion.rule_applied: The fixed conclusion rule was applied: a positive no_high_school coefficient relative to college_degree supports the focal claim; p < 0.05 indicates strong statistical evidence, while uncertainty is reported separately.
conclusion.uncertainty_statement: The estimate provides strong support because it is positive, p < 0.05, and the 95% confidence interval excludes zero in the expected positive direction.
conclusion.conclusion_text: Task2 supports the focal claim: in the pooled sample including Mexico and without prohibited controls, no-high-school immigrants had larger wage gains than college-degree immigrants.

Task2 completed successfully with the planned unadjusted trimmed OLS analysis, retained Mexico, included no prohibited controls, and required no repairs. The focal coefficient was positive and statistically significant.
